results.raw_content:
RisingshadowScience Fiction & Fantasy
 RinoZ
In the ever-evolving world of LitRPG and progression fantasy, few voices resonate quite like that of RinoZ. An Australian writer who started his journey not in the spotlight of publishing houses but in the quiet corners of web fiction forums, RinoZ carved out a name for himself with stories that do more than entertain. They pull you in, level you up, and leave you questioning the very mechanics of the worlds you thought you knew.
What sets RinoZ apart is not just his knack for crafting immersive game-like systems or his obsession with stat sheets, though both are present in spades. It is the way he uses those systems as a lens through which to explore transformation, identity, and resilience. In Chrysalis, his wildly popular debut, readers were introduced to a protagonist reborn as an ant in a dungeon teeming with danger. What could have been a quirky gimmick became something much more: a deep, often funny, sometimes unsettling exploration of what it means to evolve, not just in level but in spirit.
Read more ...
Following the success of Chrysalis, RinoZ took a darker turn with Book of the Dead, a LitRPG necromancer series that swaps the swarm for the grave. Here, the stakes feel heavier and the world grittier. Magic is not just power, it is consequence. Fans quickly latched onto Tyron, a gifted outcast navigating a brutal system that punishes those who defy its sacred rules. Through undead armies and moral ambiguity, RinoZ challenges readers to root for the kinds of characters fantasy often casts aside.
Raised on a steady diet of web novels, RinoZ came late to writing but early to worldbuilding. He often jokes that he started Chrysalis as a side project, “just to see if anyone would read it.” They did. Millions of words and a legion of fans later, he is still updating chapters, still tinkering with character builds, still obsessing over whether a summoning cooldown makes sense.
Though he prefers to let his work speak louder than interviews, RinoZ once described writing as “a dungeon crawl through your own imagination. Sometimes you find treasure. Sometimes you get eaten by a mimic.” It is this self-deprecating wit and unrelenting curiosity that keeps readers coming back, book after book.
Today, RinoZ’s books are available across Amazon, Royal Road, and Audible, consistently ranking among the top LitRPG and progression fantasy titles. For those who have followed him from the early days, he is more than just a chart-topper. He is a fellow adventurer, guiding readers through strange worlds with a torch in one hand and a stat sheet in the other.

Book of the Dead 5: Ascension
Book of the Dead Book 5
By RinoZ
Even if his heart no longer beats, Tyron will not be stopped on his path to vengeance. The Western Province has fallen, its population purged and the survivors have fled over the mountains and into a magick scoured wasteland. No matter how far they go, or how well they hide, the Empire will not rest until the heretics and rebels have been crushed.
Under the fragile leadership of Merigold Herimar, a low ranking noble appointed well above her station, the Golden Legion is massing. If she can fight through the bureaucracy and petty grievances of the court, she may save the Empire.
Tyron, knowing his options are few, must grow stronger and build his undead horde to greater heights. To achieve this, he will need to access the mysterious Realm of the Dead.
Book 5 of the next hit LitRPG series from RinoZ, the author of Chrysalis. Book of the Dead takes on all aspects of Necromancy headfirst, from the tactical manuevering of skeletons, to what it’s like spending so much time amongst the undead.

Another amazing addition to the series!
It is hard for authors to continue with the level of detail they started with when it comes to magic systems at more the advanced stages, and some of the status readings have taken a back seat here, but the author has stayed true to helping the readers understand the overall progression and strategies chosen to do so by MC. And oh how the plot progresses as well! Also love the bits of humor! Refreshingly blatant but not distracting.

While I feel that was a bit of an annoyance I’m eager for the next in the series. It’ll be too long a wait!

He's out of line, but he's right!
I love this series! It's unfortunate, really, because any other necromancy-focused story is going to be considered to this one, and that's a tough road. But it's not just the coolness of the system and the magic and the world, it's also great characters. A protagonist who is, in many ways, a villain, but the type of villain who isn't cackling evil for the hell of it, but rather motivated to do whatever is necessary to achieve his goal. He'll do the "evil," if that's what it takes, but doesn't go out of his way. Even the actual antagonists of the story have recognizable and understandable motives, if more petty and selfish. Anyway, a fantastic story and I eagerly await more!
